title: A new firefly from mid-Cretaceous Burmese amber sheds more light on the early evolution of adult bioluminescence in Lampyridae (Coleoptera: Elateroidea)
content:
Abstract
Bioluminescence serves a wide range of biological functions, including aposematism, mitigation of oxidative stress, and both interspecific and intraspecific communication. In this study, we describe a new bioluminescent firefly, Burmoluciola lesleyae Zhao, s´lipin´ski, Kundrata and Ren gen. et sp. nov., from mid-Cretaceous Kachin amber that exhibits distinctive features like serrate antennomeres 3–5, a luminous organ occupying the entire abdominal ventrite 5, and a small semicircular central area near the anterior margin on the ventrite 6. We present a comprehensive morphological phylogenetic analysis integrating extant and Mesozoic fireflies to resolve the phylogenetic placement of the fossil taxa. Our results place the earlier described Flammarionella (Cai et al.) as a sister to all sampled representatives of Luciolinae, while the new genus is nested more deeply within the subfamily. These findings enhance our understanding of the diversification of Mesozoic bioluminescent fireflies.
